issue.description:
Field evidence gathered 2026-10-23 on codinghome: a sweep of all 92 bead-rs workspaces under /home/coding, git object accounting in the largest repos, and every bead invocation in agent transcripts under ~/.claude/projects (32,149 calls) and ~/.codex/sessions (80,311 calls). Counts are regex-based and approximate.

Problem: 7 of 92 workspaces report `Git: ignored` and `Ready to commit: NO` only because leftover `.beads/checkpoint/objects/gen-*.tmp` files from interrupted publications are matched by the `*.tmp` rule in `.beads/.gitignore` (e.g. claude-print has 3; coned-rate-optimizer and git-activity-exporter 1 each). These files are not part of any published fileset, so the not-ready verdict is false. A verdict that is wrong this often trains operators to ignore it. `doctor --repair` does not remove them.

Scope:
- The Git reachability groups in `sync status` (text and JSON) consider only files in the published fileset. Temp files never appear in any group.
- `doctor` reports a stale `gen-*.tmp` as a `WARN ` line; `doctor --repair` removes it and reports a `FIXED ` line. "Stale" means no checkpoint publication lock is held and the file predates the current generation.
- Update the sync-status section of research/specs/needle-cli-contract-v1.md to say which files the groups cover.

Acceptance:
- Fixture: a published, fully committed checkpoint plus a `gen-*.tmp` debris file yields `Ready to commit: yes` and lists no ignored file.
- doctor WARNs on the debris, `--repair` removes it with a FIXED line, and a second `--repair` is a no-op.
- A temp file belonging to a publication that is in flight under the held lock is never removed (test holds the lock).
- cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo test pass.
issue.title: Exclude unpublished gen-*.tmp files from checkpoint reachability and sweep stale ones in doctor --repair

issue.description:
ADR-001 (Accepted 2026-08-12) specifies post-0.1 item R025 and no open bead covers it. Introduce a third dependency kind `verifies` so authors can declare the check relationship, and diagnose inverted verification gates structurally: report a `blocks` edge whose blocker also `verifies` the blocked bead. Constraints from the ADR: the diagnosis is advisory and reported, never rejected at insert time; the relationship is never inferred from issue titles; a deliberate prove-the-baseline-first gate is legitimate and must not be treated as an error. Cover a two-node pair that is simultaneously a cycle (rejected per §3.4) and an inversion (reported), let `bead manifest` express the `verifies` kind, and add dependency-conformance coverage per AGENTS.md's rule that no compatibility is claimed without a passing conformance suite.

---
Priority: P2
Created by: weave strand
issue.title: Implement R025: verifies dependency kind and structural inverted-gate diagnosis (ADR-001)
